subject: Taxes
title: Nixon's Tax Cheating
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nixon's Tax Cheating usable.

hook.text: President Nixon claimed a $576,000 tax deduction for donating his papers to the National Archives.

buildup.text: Congress had eliminated the deduction for donating personal papers in 1969.

discovery.text: A congressional investigation found Nixon owed $476,431 in back taxes plus interest.

twist.text: Nixon famously said: 'I am not a crook.' But his tax returns told a different story. He paid, avoiding criminal charges.

climax.text: Nixon's tax scandal showed that even the president isn't above the tax code.

punchline.text: 'I am not a crook.' His tax returns suggested otherwise.

quiz.question: What tax fraud did Nixon commit?
options: He backdated a donation to claim an expired deduction worth $576,000
He hid income in Swiss banks
